text:
A: Hello! Darren, yeah? Tomasz. You hear me okay?
B: Yeah, hiya. Fine, thanks.
A: Good, good. So what do you do, Darren? You have logo on your shirt, so I'm guessing work stuff.
B: Gas engineer. Heating firm in Halesowen. Boilers mostly.
A: Boilers! Mate, perfect, I need you. Our flat, the boiler makes this noise like, er, like knocking, every morning. Landlord says it's normal.
B: Knocking when it fires up, or when the water's running?
A: When it starts, I think. Six o'clock, bang bang, before I go to gym.
B: Could be kettling. Bit of scale on the heat exchanger, it's common in London, the water's hard. Or the pressure's off. Have a look at the gauge on the front, should be sitting about one to one and a half bar. If it's not that, it wants someone looking at, to be fair. I wouldn't leave it.
A: See, that's useful. One to one and a half. I'll tell landlord.
B: What do you do yourself?
A: I sell cars. Premium German, dealership in Park Royal. Sold three on Saturday, one of them almost ninety grand. Now I'm waiting for finance on one, the bank is being slow.
B: Right.
A: What do you drive? Personal, not the van.
B: Mostly the van, to be honest. Claire's got a Focus.
A: Focus. Okay. Good car, reliable. But you should treat yourself, mate. Nice used one, approved, the finance now is not crazy, you'd be surprised what monthly is.
B: I've got a mortgage I'm trying to pay off early, so. I'm alright with the Focus.
A: Ha, sensible man. My partner would like you.
B: Is it just the two of you?
A: Yeah, me and Hannah, nine years. No kids. You?
B: Two. Ellie's fifteen, Jack's twelve. And a spaniel.
A: Nine years, she wants to get married, kids, all that. I keep saying, after the flat. First we buy the flat.
B: Mm.
A: London prices, though. You buy in West Midlands, you get house, garden, everything, for price of a garage here.
B: We bought in 2011. Wouldn't afford it now, the way it's gone, even up our way.
A: Exactly. Football, you watch?
B: West Brom.
A: West Brom. Okay. I'm Arsenal.
B: Course you are.
A: Ha! What does that mean?
B: Nothing. Lot of London lads are.
A: I'm not London lad originally, I'm from Wrocław, Poland. Came here 2008. Arsenal was my flatmates' fault.
B: Fair enough. You've been here a while, then.
A: Sixteen years. Feels like five minutes, to be honest. You always live there, Stourbridge?
B: Born and bred. Mum's still round the corner. Sunday dinner at hers every few weeks.
A: Same with my mum, but I fly. Two, three times a year to Wrocław. She sends me photo of her dog every single day.
B: Ha. That's mums, that.
A: Every day, mate. So, the boiler, if it's the scale thing, how much is new one? Roughly. Because landlord will try and—
